themes_detail.label: Dead Animals Spike
themes_detail.summary: Central Harlem is experiencing a sharp spike in dead animal complaints THIS WEEK, with 3 reports vs. a historical weekly average of 0.5, a 500% increase that may signal environmental or pest management issues requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 3 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Coincides with elevated air quality complaints (6 last week vs. 1.9 avg) and residential disposal complaints (10 last week vs. 2.8 avg)
No corresponding news coverage or community board discussion yet—emerging issue
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: Walk streets in affected areas to document conditions and interview residents about public health concerns
Source outreach: Contact NYC Parks and NYC Health Department about pest or waste management changes in Central Harlem

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Last week saw 6 complaints of illegal tree damage in Central Harlem, a 433% spike above the 1.1 weekly average, suggesting either organized tree removal/damage or a localized environmental crisis worth documenting before evidence disappears.
evidence: 6 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% spike, z-score: 8.13)
Concurrent spike in dead/dying tree reports (3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 avg, 700% increase)
Potential connection to ULURP development activity: 254 West 124th Street and other active land use applications in district
reporting_angles: FOIL request: Obtain NYC Parks complaint details to identify specific streets and whether damage is linked to construction or development
Development angle: Cross-reference tree damage locations with active ULURP applications and DOB permits (473 filings, including 4 full demolitions)

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints spiked to 5 reports last week, a 300% increase above the 1.2 weekly baseline, representing a concerning public safety trend in Central Harlem that warrants investigation into underlying causes and community impact.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints last week vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% spike, z-score: 3.87)
No recent news coverage or community board discussion—emerging concern not yet in public discourse
Potential connection to 'Drinking' spike (3 complaints 3 weeks ago, 2300% above baseline) suggesting broader substance-use environment shift
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD precinct commander about enforcement strategy and whether 75th Precinct has observed uptick in narcotics activity
Community voices: Talk to residents, local nonprofits, and harm reduction organizations about where and when activity is occurring, and community safety impact

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Central Harlem residents filed 6 air quality complaints last week, a 220% spike above the 1.9 weekly average, potentially signaling environmental hazards from construction, traffic, or pollution that requires source identification.
evidence: 6 air quality complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (220% spike, z-score: 3.25)
Overlaps with dead animal spike (3 this week), dead/dying tree spike (3 complaints 2 weeks ago), and residential disposal spike (10 last week)
473 active DOB building permits (403 alterations) may indicate construction-related dust/emissions
reporting_angles: Source mapping: Obtain 311 complaint addresses and determine if they cluster near construction sites or major traffic corridors
Expert consultation: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection and EPA about air quality monitoring in Central Harlem and any known pollution sources

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal/Sanitation Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints reached 10 last week, a 264% spike above the 2.8 weekly average, coupled with elevated unsanitary and dirty condition complaints in the district, suggesting possible waste management breakdown or service gaps.
evidence: 10 residential disposal complaints last week vs. 2.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (264% spike, z-score: 4.23)
Baseline sanitation burden in district: 1,221 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days (highest categories: heat/hot water at 3,635, residential noise at 3,180)
Litter basket request spike 3 weeks ago (4 complaints vs. 0.4 avg, 967% increase) suggests chronic infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Service audit: Contact NYC Sanitation to determine collection schedules, staffing changes, or service disruptions in Central Harlem over past 3 weeks
Resident impact: Interview households about trash accumulation, pest problems, and what disposal challenges they're facing
